For s>1, v(s)=(1+1/s)/2 tends to 1/2. The two section kernels are bounded at the finite end b=1 and decay as O(|b|^(−d)) at the negative end, so they are absolutely integrable for d≥2. Their truncated integrals multiplied by 1/(2s) tend to zero. The cap formula then gives P(s)→V/2. An atom at infinity has zero moment, so the conditional finite law is centered whenever its mass is positive. Its corrected average mixes with V/2, and the pure infinity case directly gives V/2.

Multiply the corrected lower inequality for μ by C̄ν and the corrected upper inequality for ν by C̄μ. Subtraction cancels the common coefficient c, and adding VC̄μ gives the oriented numerator with lower bound (4/9)V(C̄μ+C̄ν). The division assumes positive total coarea. The derivative of log Γ_x=−x log(1+1/x) is strictly negative because log(1+y)>y/(1+y) for y>0, so Γ_d≤Γ_2=4/9.

Every finite layer has strictly positive C by positivity of its kernel and captured probability, so an averaged C of zero means a pure infinity law. If one coarea vanishes, the remaining term in the quotient evaluates its corresponding infinity cap fraction or complement, both 1/2. For finite laws, P̄/V−1/2=p0e−(v−1/2), and 0≤v−1/2≤e/2, giving the stated bound (p0+1/2)C̄/C0 in absolute value without centering. Averaging with the infinity record preserves it. For fixed cone parameters the quotient is a convex combination of P̄μ/V and 1−P̄ν/V, and both approach 1/2 as the respective coareas approach zero, proving continuity in the records even for unbounded finite slopes.

As an independent check of the constants, take d=2 and H=2, so a0=1/3 and c=0. For s=3, v=2/3 and e(q)=[(1/3)(1+1/3)]/[2(1−q)(1/3+q)] has its minimum at q=1/3 with value 1/2. This single layer is centered and P/V=5/9. The centered horizontal layer has P/V=4/9. Using the horizontal layer for μ and s=3 for ν gives quotient 4/9.

The bound is for two separately centered laws on one full affine cone. The actual frustum transfer in f26ba90707244e98 yields β_f=(β_c−tω)/(1−t) for bounded representatives, with ω=Cν/(Cμ+Cν). A lower bound on β_c alone leaves the subtraction term to account for, and the reviewed statement draws no conclusion for that frustum or for other profiles.
